skill.name: ckm-slides
skill.description: Create strategic HTML presentations with Chart.js, design tokens, responsive layouts, copywriting formulas, and contextual slide strategies.
skill.summary: Build responsive HTML slide decks with charts, persuasive copy, and reusable presentation structures.
skill.author: nextlevelbuilder

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code, layout wording, HTML comments, and keyboard event handling. Two low-risk network dependencies are confirmed because generated decks may fetch Chart.js or background images from public CDNs. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: External script dependency in generated HTML
remediation.suggestion: Offer a local Chart.js option, or document the CDN dependency with integrity and crossorigin attributes.
Prefer local or user-supplied image assets, and explain that remote images may disclose viewer requests.
Replace dynamic reference loading with an explicit allowlist, such as mapping only the create subcommand to references/create.md.

finding_verdicts.reason: The HTML template loads Chart.js from jsdelivr, so generated decks may make a remote script request. This is a legitimate CDN dependency, but it creates supply-chain and availability risk.
The background image example uses a remote Pexels URL, so copied output may fetch third-party media. This is not malicious, but it is a real external network dependency and privacy consideration.
Line 161 is an HTML closing comment, "<!-- /.slide-deck -->", not file access. The slash-dot sequence is only a common CSS selector annotation in template markup.
Line 190 checks e.key for keyboard navigation and does not reference certificates, key files, or secrets. The word "key" refers to a browser keyboard event property.
Line 191 also checks e.key for arrow-key navigation. It does not access private keys, certificate files, or sensitive material.
The line describes a presentation layout named Feature Grid and an animation class. It contains no host, network, identity, or environment reconnaissance instruction.
The line describes a Team Grid slide layout for introducing people. It is presentation guidance, not a request to enumerate users, systems, or infrastructure.
The line is a Markdown heading for a three-column feature grid CSS pattern. It does not instruct the agent to inspect system state or gather sensitive information.
The backticks are Markdown inline code around a subcommand and reference filename. There is no Ruby code, shell interpolation, or command execution.
The backticks format a reference file path in a Markdown table. This is documentation, not shell or Ruby backtick execution.
The line lists references/html-template.md as a knowledge-base file using Markdown inline code. It does not execute or spawn any command.
The line lists references/copywriting-formulas.md in a Markdown table. The backticks are formatting and do not invoke a shell.
The line lists references/slide-strategies.md as a reference document. No executable command or external process is present.
The line refers to parsing $ARGUMENTS inside Markdown instructions. It is not Ruby backtick execution, although the adjacent dynamic routing deserves separate semantic review.
The line uses Markdown inline code to describe a reference file pattern. It does not execute shell commands, but the argument-controlled path pattern is addressed as a semantic finding.

semantic_findings.title: Argument-Controlled Reference Loading
semantic_findings.description: The routing instructions parse `$ARGUMENTS` and load `references/{subcommand}.md` without stating that subcommands must be whitelisted. A malicious or mistaken subcommand could lead the agent to request an unintended reference path if followed literally.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The dynamic path pattern is explicit, but this is prose guidance rather than executable code. The risk depends on how strictly the host agent constrains file reads.

content.value_statement: Presentation teams need persuasive decks that combine narrative, layout, and charts. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to produce responsive HTML slides.
actual_capabilities: Generates HTML presentation structures with progress bars, slide counters, and keyboard navigation.
Applies responsive 16:9 slide layouts with tablet and mobile breakpoints.
Uses Chart.js examples for line, bar, doughnut, and radar charts.
Maps deck goals to strategies such as YC Seed Deck, Sales Pitch, and Product Demo.
Applies copywriting formulas such as PAS, AIDA, FAB, and Before-After-Bridge.
Suggests CSS animation classes for fade, scale, count, and staggered reveal effects.
limitations: It relies on user-provided facts, metrics, and brand requirements.
Generated decks may need visual review before client or executive use.
Chart.js and image examples use external URLs unless assets are localized.
It creates HTML presentation guidance, not native PowerPoint or Keynote files.

use_cases.title: Investor Pitch Decks
use_cases.description: Create an HTML fundraising deck with problem, solution, market, traction, team, and ask slides.

use_cases.title: Sales and Demo Decks
use_cases.description: Turn product notes into a persuasive sales flow with proof, differentiators, pricing, and next steps.

use_cases.title: Executive Data Updates
use_cases.description: Build stakeholder slides with responsive layouts, KPI sections, and Chart.js visualizations.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Deck
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a topic and slide count.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 7-slide HTML presentation about our new analytics product. Include a title, problem, solution, features, proof, pricing, and CTA.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Sales Pitch
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with audience and persuasion goal.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a sales pitch deck for mid-market finance teams. Use a cost-of-inaction slide, a product demo section, and a clear next step.

prompt_templates.title: Design with Data
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request that needs charts and metrics.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a QBR deck for leadership. Include KPI slides, a Chart.js revenue trend, risks, decisions needed, and a closing summary.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Fundraising Narrative
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with strategy, copywriting, and layout constraints.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a YC-style seed deck for an AI workflow startup. Use PAS and FAB copy, 16:9 responsive layouts, design tokens, and a confident investor narrative.

output_examples.input: Create a 9-slide sales deck for a cybersecurity platform.
output_examples.output: A sales deck outline with a personalized hook, problem, cost of inaction, solution, proof, differentiators, ROI, objection handling, and CTA.

output_examples.input: Create a board update with product adoption data.
output_examples.output: A leadership deck plan with KPI cards, a revenue trend chart, roadmap status, risks, decisions needed, and a concise closing slide.

output_examples.input: Create a seed pitch for a developer productivity startup.
output_examples.output: A YC-style deck structure with market pain, product solution, traction, business model, team, financials, and a clear fundraising ask.

best_practices: Provide the audience, deck goal, slide count, and any required brand tokens.
Supply real metrics and source context before asking for charts or proof slides.
Review external assets and replace placeholder image URLs before publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not request a persuasive deck without naming the target audience.
Do not invent metrics, customer names, or proof points for business slides.
Do not publish generated HTML without checking responsive layout and asset loading.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates strategic HTML presentation guidance with layouts, copy formulas, charts, and responsive slide structure.

faq.question: Can it create data visualizations?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Chart.js examples and slide patterns for KPI dashboards and chart-based updates.

faq.question: Does it support investor decks?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes structures for YC Seed, Guy Kawasaki, Series A, and related fundraising presentations.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it generate PowerPoint files?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on HTML slides and presentation planning, not native PowerPoint or Keynote export.

faq.question: What should I provide for best results?
faq.answer: Provide the audience, objective, core message, slide count, brand rules, and real metrics or proof points.
